newsitem.title: CHINA: China Xinjiang earthquake injury toll rises to 40.
newsitem.headline: China Xinjiang earthquake injury toll rises to 40.

text.p: Thousands of families had been forced to flee their homes after two earthquakes that killed 12 people and injured more than 40 in China's northwestern Xinjiang region, an official said on Wednesday.

At least 12 people were killed on Tuesday when an earthquake measuring 6.4 on the open-ended Richter scale struck Xinjiang, followed one minute later by a tremor measuring 6.3, an official with the Xinjiang Seismological Bureau said.
More than 9,500 houses had collapsed and more than 20,000 houses were damaged in the earthquakes, the official said by telephone.
An unknown number of people had been left homeless by the earthquakes, and most were now living in tents in freezing temperatures, the official said.
"The army and relief teams have already sent out supplies, food and tents," she said.
The earthquakes, which struck the Jiashi and Artux districts that are populated mainly by sheep herders and cotton farmers, had killed about 3,500 head of livestock, she said.
Officials had yet to calculate economic losses, she said.
The number of casualties could rise as rescue teams and officials searched through rubble of collapsed houses, officials have said.
State radio quoted seismological officials as predicting that an earthquake of 5.5 magnitude could strike the same area in the near future.
An earthquake of 6.9 magnitude rocked Jiashi last March, killing 26 people and injuring 128.
